class.name: IfcRelInterferesElements
class.brief_description: Definition from IAI : The IfcRelInterferesElements objectified relationship indicates that two elements interfere. Interference is a spatial overlap between the two elements. It is a 1 to 1 relationship. The concept of two elements interfering physically or logically is described independently from the elements. The interference may be related to the shape representation of the entities by providi
class.description: Only in IFC4 and IFC4X3_ADD2 files.

members.member: Reference to a subtype of IfcElement that is the RelatingElement in the interference relationship. Depending on the value of ImpliedOrder the RelatingElement may carry the notion to be the element from which the interference geometry should be subtracted. Only in IFC4 and IFC4X3_ADD2 files: in others it reads as null and can't be set.

Reference to a subtype of IfcElement that is the RelatedElement in the interference relationship. Depending on the value of ImpliedOrder the RelatedElement may carry the notion to be the element from which the interference geometry should not be subtracted. Only in IFC4 and IFC4X3_ADD2 files: in others it reads as null and can't be set.

The geometric shape representation of the interference geometry that is provided in the object coordinate system of the RelatingElement (mandatory) and in the object coordinate system of the RelatedElement (optionally). Only in IFC4 and IFC4X3_ADD2 files: in others it reads as null and can't be set.

Optional identifier that describes the nature of the interference. Examples could include 'Clash', 'ProvisionForVoid', etc. A String, or null when unset. Only in IFC4 and IFC4X3_ADD2 files: in others it reads as null and can't be set.

Logical value indicating whether the interference geometry should be subtracted from the RelatingElement (if TRUE), or whether it should be either subtracted from the RelatingElement or the RelatedElement (if FALSE), or whether no indication can be provided (if UNKNOWN). A String ("TRUE", "FALSE" or "UNKNOWN"), or null when unset. Only in IFC4 and IFC4X3_ADD2 files: in others it reads as null and can't be set.
Only in IFC4X3_ADD2 files: in others it reads as null and can't be set.
